From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Annual planning charter + decision-path: initial plan and asks

Team —

I want to start a short, focused planning sprint to lock targets and a decision-path for the FY26 QBR/annual plan. Attached is a first-pass planning charter (planning-charter-v1.pdf). High level:

- Objective: arrive at a set of target bands (conservative/base/aggressive) and a single decision calendar with clear owners and trigger thresholds.
- Timeline: 3 weeks (draft targets + scenarios by week 1; finance validation week 2; leadership review week 3).
- Key outputs: target bands, scenario matrix (capacity/cost/quality), decision calendar (dates & gating criteria), and a short QBR-ready slide set.

Immediate asks (please):
1) By end of Wed 3/17 — each owner to name 2 levers they can move (e.g., pricing, dedicated capacity, feature gating) and a rough impact estimate. Owner list below.
2) By Fri 3/19 — submit a one-paragraph assumption list (headcount, ARR growth, churn, unit economics).
3) Marissa/Finance: run a quick run-rate vs committed capacity sensitivity (token cost assumptions).
4) Soojin/Product Ops: draft scenario matrix template (I'll attach a CSV placeholder after replies).

Proposed coordination: 60m working session Thu 3/18 10:00 PT to align on scope and owners — please confirm availability.

Drive links + doc in the footer. I intentionally kept the charter concise to avoid over-optimization at this stage.

Attachments: planning-charter-v1.pdf (charter, objectives, timeline)

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Product Operations

Thanks Marcus — this is the right level of focus. A couple of small requests from my side:

- Please include explicit headcount assumptions in the assumption list template. We should avoid re-running scenarios that contradict hiring plans.
- Add a short section in the charter for near-term commercial levers: channel marketplace push, reserved capacity pricing, and enterprise pilot cadence. Those are where we can pull upside quickly.
- For the working session on 3/18, can we reserve the first 20m for a quick review of QBR-ready metrics (ARR by cohort, new logo contribution, retention cohorts)?

I don't have attachments — I'll drop a brief QBR prep outline to the Drive after lunch.

Echo Laura's ask. A couple of operational guardrails to add here:

- Decision thresholds: recommend we codify 3 explicit gating criteria for any upward target revision — customer commit velocity, committed reserved revenue, and a 60-day execution confidence check.
- Cost sensitivity: Marissa, please prepare a short table of cost per 1M tokens under current mix (hosted vs dedicated), and a variant assuming 10% and 25% more quantized model mix. We need this to decide whether to lean into dedicated capacity as a growth lever.
- Timing: I can make Thu 3/18 10:00 PT. If that fills up, alternate 3/19 9:00 PT works.

Also — looping Stephanie to help track owners and decision outcomes in the tracker (Stephanie — would you own the decision calendar doc and follow ups?).

—Vivek

Thanks — quick notes from Product Ops perspective.

- I'll scaffold the scenario-matrix with three vectors: demand (low/base/high), model mix (hosted/dedicated/quantized), and quality/regression risk (guardrails). I'll attach scenario-matrix.csv.
- For the decision calendar, we must include an evaluation baseline: a holdout prompt set and response-quality pass rate (we should not trade >0.5% delta in user-facing quality across scenarios without explicit signoff).
- Suggest owners for the levers:
  - Pricing adjustments: Laura
  - Dedicated capacity ramp plan: Marissa
  - Product gating / feature rollout pace: Soojin

I'll upload the CSV and a short explanation in Drive by EOD.
